Say where the access message reaches the person

mail_access_recipients.Rd

To contact_email, as the welcome, when it is outside the tenant's domain. When it is inside, decision 12 makes it the UPN, and the UPN is not where the person reads mail: for most accounts of the tenant it has no mailbox, Exchange Online refuses the message ("550 5.4.1 Recipient address rejected: Access denied"), and the mail service then suppresses the address and drops every later send to it in silence, while it still answers 202 and accessi_recapitati still counts it. So the message goes, decided on 2026-11-10, to the account's mailbox and to its first external address, both read by the sweep (directory_mailboxes()) and carried here by identified: to both in one message when both are there, the same address once.

Usage

mail_access_recipients(row, domain = "ubep.unipd.it")

Arguments

row

One register row as a list, with mailbox and external as the round settled them.

domain

The tenant's verified domain, as identity_internal() takes it.

Value

A character vector: the contact as written when it is external, possibly empty; otherwise the mailbox and the external address that are there, without duplicates, possibly none. NULL for an internal contact on a row that does not carry mailbox or external.

Details

Nothing when neither is: the caller then sends the message to the referent, who tells the person (mail_access_message()). Never the UPN alone, for the reason above.

A row that does not carry the two fields is another case, and not the same as one that carries them empty: the round did not say where the account reads mail, so nobody knows it has nowhere. NULL says so, and the caller loses the message, as a row without an address loses it, rather than tell the referent something nobody read.
